evidence.details: Missing markdown content negotiation. findings.summary: ora.ai check "MCP server-card.json" (mcp-server-card) reported status "fail"

evidence.details: No MCP server card found (checked /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json, the site's ai-catalog.json, servers[].card in mcp.json, and <server>/server-card)
evidence.recommendation: Publish a server card for each MCP server (draft MCP server-card extension). List each card in /.well-known/ai-catalog.json, or serve it at <server URL>/server-card. /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json is still read for a site with one server, but the extension does not recommend it. Include name, description, and version, and put the server's exact address in remotes[].url (serverUrl is also read) so agents match each card to the right server before connecting. Follow the extension schema for full credit: $schema set to https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/v1/server-card.schema.json, a reverse-DNS name such as com.example/mcp, and no tools[] (agents always trust the live tools/list). Keep the description to 100 characters or fewer, as the schema requires. A card without that $schema is still read, and then an optional tools[] list completes it.

unmapped.details: Not published
unmapped.recommendation: Reject unauthenticated agents in the shape PAP defines. Your token endpoint should answer a session request (the RFC 7523 JWT grant) it cannot verify with one of the codes the spec lists: invalid_client (401), invalid_grant (400), or invalid_dpop_proof (400) when the DPoP proof is missing. The conversation endpoint should return 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate: DPoP` challenge when no token is sent, and an MCP server that needs a token should answer a request without one with 401 and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<your /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource URL>"`, plus a DPoP challenge with the same resource_metadata when the server supports DPoP. The browser_session_endpoint should answer an invalid assertion with 400 and set no cookie, the operations endpoint should return 401 without a token, and a feedback endpoint should refuse a report sent with no token with 401 and a `WWW-Authenticate: DPoP` challenge. Answer the token, API, conversation, feedback and operations endpoints at the address you publish, without redirects, and require a DPoP proof with every token endpoint request and every request that carries a Session Token. The exception is an MCP server that does not support DPoP: requesting its Bearer token, and using it, needs no proof. Revocation and device authorization requests are neither, so they need no proof. Spec: https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/spec
